name: What are the tradeoffs between patching an existing door jamb versus replacing the whole frame?

mainEntity.name: What are the tradeoffs between patching an existing door jamb versus replacing the whole frame?

acceptedAnswer.text: Patching the existing frame saves money and preserves existing trim, while full replacement provides structural longevity and eliminates hidden moisture issues. Splicing in a Dutchman patch is ideal when damage is confined strictly to the bottom corner of a jamb, reducing disturbance to adjoining tile, drywall, or custom paint. However, older frames that have experienced repeated swelling can remain out of square, causing ongoing sticking or latching issues. Installing a completely new frame takes longer and costs more upfront, but it ensures a plumb opening, tight weather or privacy seals, and fresh, rot-free materials.
acceptedAnswer.description: Patching preserves existing trim and costs less, but replacing the entire frame guarantees a plumb fit and removes hidden mold or rot behind the jamb.
